plain_text:
Ad-Hoc City Manager Search Committee 
Draft Meeting Minutes 
October 29, 2026  
City Council Chambers 
37 Green Street  
6:00 PM 
1. Mayor Champlin called the meeting to order at 6:02 p.m. 
 
2. Roll Call.  
Present: Mayor Champlin, Councilors Brown, Davie, Fennessy, Horne, Kalob, Keach, 
Kretovic, Kurtz, Sekou 
 
Excused: Councilors Foote, Grady-Sexton, Schlosser, Schultz, Todd 
 
Staff Members Present: John Conforti City Solicitor and Jennifer Johnston Director of 
Human Resources and Labor Relations.  
 
3. Meeting Overview. 
 
Mayor Champlin provided an overview of the items to be discussed, including meeting with 
Jennifer Johnston, Director of Human Resources and Labor Relations, to review the results 
of the anonymous employee City Manager survey, review the scoring rubric for the search 
firms, and establish an interview schedule for the search firm respondents. 
 
4. Approval of Meeting Minutes. 
 
Councilor Horne moved approval of the September 28, 2026 Draft Meeting Minutes. The 
motion was duly seconded by Councilor Kretovic and passed unanimously. 
 
5. Report on Results of Employee Survey.  
 
Jennifer Johnston, Director of Human Resources and Labor Relations, reviewed the results 
of the employee survey conducted through SurveyMonkey. The survey received 118 
responses, representing a 25% employee participation rate. The survey results are available 
on the City’s website.

Director Johnston summarized the key themes from employee feedback, which emphasized 
the importance of having a City Manager who is visible, approachable, communicative, and 
responsive. Employees expressed the importance of transparency in decision-making, 
consistent accountability, effective departmental leadership, and meaningful opportunities to 
contribute to the City’s success. 
 
The overarching message reflected employees’ desire for leadership that builds trust through 
engagement and demonstrates commitment through action. Key priorities for the incoming 
City Manager include maintaining regular communication, actively listening to employees, 
following through on commitments, supporting department heads, and fostering a 
collaborative and inclusive organizational culture. 
 
Council members expressed their appreciation for the survey and noted its value in 
informing the City Manager search process. Mayor Champlin stated that the Council would 
request that the survey be posted on the City’s website, as it is a public document. Council 
also requested that the survey results be distributed to employees via email and made 
available through the employee portal. 
 
6. Review of Evaluation Scoring Sheet for Search Firm Respondents. 
 
Director Johnston reviewed the proposed scoring rubric for evaluating the search firm 
proposals. The rubric allocates 60% of the score to the firm’s experience and capacity, 35% 
to its proposed recruitment and search plan, and whether the proposal meets the 
requirements outlined in the Request for Proposals (RFP). 
 
Director Johnston reported that the City had received nine responses to the City Manager 
Search RFP, one of which was eliminated for failing to meet the stated requirements. She 
explained that the process was structured as a closed bid process, meaning the cost 
proposals would not be reviewed until the Committee determined which submissions met 
the RFP requirements. 
 
Director Johnston explained that the Council would need to establish the procedure for 
opening the bids, specifically whether they would be opened before or after the search firm 
interviews. The Council would also need to determine the evaluation criteria for the third 
scoring category. 
 
The Council discussed the merits of both approaches, including conducting interviews 
before opening the bids and opening the bids prior to interviews. 
 
Director Johnston suggested that the third evaluation category could address the firms’ 
proposed approach to community engagement. Councilor Kretovic noted that the previous 
City Manager search included input from area representatives of larger corporations, 
developers, and business-sector CEOs and presidents. Mayor Champlin further noted that it 
would be important to ask the firms about their proposed processes and timelines and how 
community engagement could be incorporated into the overall search process.

7. Establishment of Interview Schedule for Shortlisted Respondents. 
 
Director Johnston reported that she had drafted interview questions for the search firms, 
which will be shared exclusively with the Committee. The Committee agreed that a non-
public meeting would be held to finalize the questions. Director Johnston noted that Council 
feedback could be discussed during the November 9 non-public City Council meeting. 
 
The Committee reviewed the proposed interview schedule and timeline. The next 
Committee meeting is scheduled for November 12 at 6:00 pm. The Committee discussed 
beginning search firm interviews on that date, with approximately 45 minutes allocated per 
firm and 15–20 minutes between interviews to allow for review and discussion. 
 
The Committee agreed to discuss the process for hiring an interim City Manager during its 
November 16 non-public meeting. Director Johnston asked the Committee whether the 
search firms could also assist in filling an interim City Manager position, and the Council 
agreed that this could be included as a question during the firm interviews. 
 
8. Adjournment. 
 
Councilor Fennessy moved to adjourn the meeting at 7:17 p.m.  The motion was duly 
seconded by Councilor Kretovic and passed with no dissenting votes. 
 
 
 
 
A true copy, I attest: 
 
 
Deborah Tuite 
Deputy City Clerk
